q: A state-changing step times out and the approved effect might already exist. What happens before any repeat?
options: Send the operation again and rely on the newest result
Treat the remote service as having rejected the request
Drop the action record and start a different workflow for the same intent
Reconcile by the stable effect identity
explanation: A timeout can hide a successful effect and does not prove failure.

q: What does a safe playbook define first?
options: The full set of actions a connector could technically perform
The default severity for every alert from unrelated sources
The intended effect, boundaries and authority
A presentation label for the latest workflow revision
explanation: A bounded purpose gives every following step an explicit operating context.

q: A notification fails after a training task was verified. What is the proper recovery?
options: Run the entire workflow again to create another task
Keep the task and retry or hand off just the notification
Remove the existing task because one related step failed
Assume the reviewer was informed when the task was created
explanation: Partial completion is reconciled by individual effect, not whole-run status.

q: What makes an effect key useful for a duplicate check?
options: It represents the same intended change across attempts
It is a separate random value assigned to each delivery
It matches the display label of any related asset
It includes the current network response time by default
explanation: A stable intent key lets the system identify repeat effects.

q: A service returns a target identifier different from the approved target. What should the workflow do?
options: Accept the effect because the response contained any target value
Replace the approval record with the returned target to make it match
Apply the same change to the original target without checking the first effect
Stop later changes and record the mismatch for review
explanation: A successful receipt cannot establish a valid effect on an unapproved object.

q: Which playbook outcome is valid even when it produces no change?
options: Silent removal of unresolved events from the audit trail
An assumed failure that needs no evidence or follow-up
A scoped review with an explicit reason and owner
A restarted workflow that creates new effects for the same request
explanation: Stopping with a review state can be an intended safe result.

q: Both an inventory lookup and an approval check are unavailable. Which could allow partial progress?
options: Record both failures as successful checks to avoid losing the case
Continue approved case preparation and stop the gated change
Approve the step automatically because neither dependency made a decision
Discard all work and remove the record of the original input
explanation: Preparation can proceed in a bounded way while authority is still unverified.

q: What should a recovery note name after a partial failure?
options: Known effects, unresolved outcomes and responsible owners
Only the latest status colour of the entire workflow
Every unreviewed credential used by unrelated integrations
The original plan without any updated observations
explanation: Recovery depends on knowing which effects actually occurred and who handles the rest.

q: A pause is set due to incorrect downstream routing. What should happen to valid incoming alerts?
options: Drop them until the owner restarts the automation
Mark them all complete because the workflow is paused
Replay them later without checking for earlier effects
Preserve them and route time-sensitive work for manual review
explanation: A pause can stop state changes while preserving legitimate work.

q: What belongs in each audit entry for a consequential operation?
options: A single summary saying that the automation owner was available
A copy of every credential used during approval
Decision reference, version, scope, effect identity and outcome
The entire source event store even if the action used one record
explanation: Reviewers need the inputs and results of the particular action.

q: The proposed change cannot be fully reversed after information is disclosed. What should the plan address?
options: A blanket promise that a rollback restores all prior state
Prevention and review of the irreversible consequence
Preservation of a wider permission for future emergency use
The ability to delete the log showing which information left
explanation: A recovery plan must account for effects outside its ability to undo.

q: Why separate training from operational permissions?
options: So a simulated test cannot accidentally affect real assets
So all integration credentials can be identical across environments
So trained operators do not need to review production changes
So validation can accept any scope supplied by the exercise input
explanation: Isolation should be enforced by scope and credentials, not just labels.

q: A repeated input has a different timestamp but the same authorised operation. What should be verified?
options: Whether the timestamps sort into different calendar minutes
Whether the original case was created by a different operator
Whether the newer audit entry can overwrite the older evidence
Whether the existing effect answers the same intent
explanation: A new receipt time alone does not create a new intended effect.

q: What is the best purpose of a retry limit?
options: Ensure every approved action retries until it eventually executes
Prevent any analyst from seeing failures while the queue is busy
Contain temporary recovery attempts and expose persistent failure
Convert an unknown outcome into a successful status after several tries
explanation: Bounded recovery and accountable review avoid indefinite unsafe repetition.

q: A verified effect lacks a required approval reference. How should this be handled?
options: Accept the result because the technical effect is already complete
Investigate it as an unexpected control outcome
Assign the latest available approval even if it concerns another case
Treat the missing reference as unrelated to operating scope
explanation: Verification does not excuse missing authority for a gated action.

q: Which outcome should a malformed target produce?
options: Input review without a state change
An effect on the closest matching display name
A successful change under the last known approval
A different default operation that tolerates missing scope
explanation: The actual target is a prerequisite for the specific approved effect.

q: An effect was never started before the workflow paused. What does resuming require?
options: Apply it automatically because it appeared before the pause
Rewrite it with a new effect identity to bypass prior review
Remove it from the case and silently confirm it was completed
Check whether its scope and authorisation are still current
explanation: Elapsed time and case changes can invalidate an earlier plan.

q: Who should own a safe playbook's design and changes?
options: Any end user who originally noticed a case event
The environment with the highest number of executed actions
A designated workflow owner with review responsibilities
The first tool whose result appears in the run history
explanation: Ownership makes testing, repair and permission changes accountable.

q: An approved request was accepted but no outcome has appeared. What should a case note distinguish?
options: The severity assigned to the case from the name of the workflow
An acknowledged request from a verified effect
The prior version of the test fixture from the future upgrade date
The operating label from the address displayed by the incident report
explanation: Acceptance does not confirm that the target has applied the change.

q: What should be preserved after an unexpected branch failure?
options: The reason, case reference and state already observed
Only the planned effects that now seem likely
A replaced input whose values fit the desired outcome
A copied successful result from an unrelated execution
explanation: Evidence of failure is needed to continue or reconcile safely.

q: A source repeatedly sends invalid data after a mapping change. What is the safest repair approach?
options: Disable validation until the queue becomes smaller
Accept every new value by assuming it is authorised
Ask the source to overwrite old records so they no longer fail
Pause affected effects and test a reviewed mapping with original fixtures
explanation: Repair should preserve the safety boundary and regression evidence.

q: What need does a separate restoration decision address?
options: Permission for any employee to reverse every response operation
Automatic erasure of all case history on return to service
Accountability for ending or compensating a protective change
Avoiding any record of how the change affected evidence
explanation: Restoration can affect real systems and needs its own verified criteria.

q: Two effects have the same case and target but different approved scopes. What helps preserve them correctly?
options: Force them to share one key because the case is the same
Identify each distinct intent in its effect identity
Treat both as duplicate receipts if display names match
Assign all effects based on who happened to be on shift
explanation: An effect key should include distinctions important to the actual operation.

q: Why test both denied and verified paths?
options: To confirm the boundary and the intended allowed result
To guarantee the workflow must always make a state change
To remove manual ownership from the application review
To classify any delayed service as untrustworthy automatically
explanation: Negative and positive tests together show what the workflow permits.

q: Which role decides whether a paused protective action still makes sense?
options: The queue scheduler because its timestamps are newer
The first service able to run the action without review
The most recent participant to look at the alert title
The authorised incident lead using current context
explanation: An operational decision needs current case scope and accountable authority.
